conclusion.decision: Yes. Showing what the app does is better than today's tour, so the new onboarding shows three features working, one after another, made from the person's own answers. After two quick taps (their goal and the foods they avoid) they see real dishes at a restaurant they go to, with that restaurant's own figures. After they pick their supermarket, they see two of our recipes priced there. After their daily targets, they see a real week of meals from their shop on one shopping list. Would plain feature screens (pictures of the app, one per feature) be better? Honestly, no: people swipe past them, a picture can't show anyone their own numbers, and its figures go out of date, so that format becomes the App Store screenshots, which people see before they download. The tab tour, Pip's separate hello screen, the "Look around first" choice and "You're all set!" all go. The free account comes last (step 11 of 11) and Home opens with their first recipe waiting. Nothing is sold during setup, no reviews, users or numbers are invented, and all of it ships in the next build: build 7 in review is not touched.

How the room rates it, out of 10:

TODAY'S ONBOARDING (with last night's fixes): 6.0, Pip 6.5.

- The most persuasive screen (two recipes from your shop, which 10 of 16 testers liked most) comes last.

THE TWO DRAFTS, averaged over the three reviews: A 7.5 (7.6, 7.5, 7.5); B 7.1 (8.1, 6.8, 6.5).
- All three reviewers asked for a merge, two of them with A as the base.
- B was richer, but it got the Maintain and GLP-1 headings wrong, removed the approved later-day trial sheet, and carried more text and controls than older readers manage.

THE CHOSEN DESIGN: 8.2 expected, Pip 7.8.
- 'Shows what the app does for me': 3 to 9.
- 'An ordinary or older person finishes': 7 to 8.
- 'Honest and within the rules': 8 to 9.
- Why it scores higher:
  - The first real figure comes at touch 4, about 20 to 30 seconds in.
  - Three features are shown working with the person's own goal, shop and numbers.
  - Every question pays off on the next screen or the one after.
  - There is one counter that never restarts.
  - The account is asked for after value has been shown.
  - Home opens with something of theirs already waiting.

WHAT HOLDS IT BELOW 9:
- Everyone must still sign in, so the App Store 5.1.1(v) risk is unchanged.
- Scan your food can only be described, never shown, because an estimate may only come from the person's own photo.
- Tesco shoppers (3 recipes) and Lidl shoppers (0) see another shop's recipes, though step 4 now tells them so in advance.

These scores are forecasts. The room trusts them only after the Round 4 test (5 people over 60, at least two of them using VoiceOver or Zoom) and after App Store Connect's day-1 and day-7 retention for the next build has been compared with build 7.

conclusion.feature_screens:
HOW THEY ARE MADE: live components only, never pictures.
Each feature screen is a thin wrapper over the app's own code, reading the same pipeline menus and shop files at render time:
- Eat out (step 3): lib/mm/truth/presets.ts applyPreset for the goal's Quick answer, after the app's own filter (passesPreferences), keeping the free top 2 (FREE_PRESET_RESULTS).
- Recipes (step 5): the existing RecipeChoice, pickTwoRecipes and RecipeTile, with a new choose mode.
- Your week (step 10): Meal plan's own planning (planCandidates, mergeCandidates, planForBudget in lib/mm/mealPlan.ts), moved into one shared helper, lib/mm/planPreview.ts, that Meal plan also uses, so the preview and the real screen can never disagree.

There are no screenshots, phone frames, baked-in figures, example numbers or count-up animations. A bezel inside the web view would shrink 17 pt text to about 10 pt, ignore the logo switches and hidden.json, freeze menus and prices the day they change, and look tappable when it isn't.

HOW THEY LOOK
- Each sits in a 'window': a full-size white card with the 1 px #d9dedb line and 20 px corners.
- It is flat (no lift shadow) wherever its contents can't be tapped (steps 3 and 10). Step 5's recipe tiles keep the lifted style because tapping them chooses one.
- A caption row with the real tab icon in a page-fill well says 'A look at Eat out', 'A look at Recipes' or 'A look at Meal plan, on Home'. It teaches where each feature lives without a tour, and says plainly that it is a preview.
- Captions are at least 15 px at 4.5:1. The Free and Premium tags always carry their word, never colour alone.
- One full-width ink button per screen. Headlines are 2rem, so the first content sits above the sticky button at 375x667.
- Chip swaps crossfade in 180 ms inside a fixed minimum height, and the window fades in over 200 ms. All of it is still under Reduce Motion. No dots, swipes or auto-advance.

WHAT EACH SHOWS (the founder's 'feature one, then this, then that', each straight after the question that shapes it)
1. Know before you order (free, after goal and foods avoided):
   - up to four chips, one per kind of place (fast food, bakery and sandwiches, coffee shops, sit-down), the first already chosen;
   - two real dishes from the goal's list, each with the restaurant's own kcal, protein and published serving;
   - the source line with its date, and 'Not affiliated with {chain}.'
2. Recipes from {shop} (free, after the shop): two of our recipes made from that shop's labelled, priced products, with kcal, macros, '£x a serving' and minutes. Tapping one makes it 'Your first recipe', which waits on Home.
3. Your week, planned (Premium where sold, after the targets): one person's real week at their shop and numbers, shown as Monday's three meals, the daily average against their target and 'Shopping for the week at {shop}: about £{total}'. Scan your food, Make it at home and Cook with what you already have are named in one line, only where switched on.

SHOWING THE CUSTOMER
Each window mirrors the person's own answers: 'Under 500 calories at Greggs', 'Dishes that list peanuts ... are left out', 'Recipes from Sainsbury's', 'sized to your numbers', 'your target is 1,850 kcal'. No testimonials, user counts, ratings, reviews, invented people or weight-loss projection charts, ever.

RULE 1 SAFEGUARDS (no invented numbers)
- Every figure is computed when the screen draws.
- Skeletons and fallbacks contain no digits. A unit test feeds each showcase empty or failed data and checks that no digit is drawn.
- Missing optional nutrients say 'not published'.
- Counts in copy ('{n} restaurants') come from the data.
- The copy says 'the restaurant's own published figures', because only 123 of 241 real chains publish protein, and the chips offer only chains that do.
- Prices always carry the shelf-price line.
- Scan your food is described, never demonstrated: an example estimate would be an AI number outside the Scan screen.
- Recipes on step 5 are shown as written (no target until step 9), so nothing is sized to numbers that aren't the person's.

RULE 2 SAFEGUARDS (logos and pictures)
- Chain and shop logos appear only as the app already shows them: under appLogos with hidden.json honoured, unmodified on white tiles, with the name always written beside them (alt="").
- No chain food photos on any onboarding screen; they stay on the real dish pages with their caption.
- Recipe illustrations are our own, carry no visible caption, and screen readers hear 'An illustration of {recipe}'.
- 'Not affiliated with {chain}.' sits under every dish, and the cover keeps 'Not affiliated with any restaurant or shop shown.'
- These onboarding screens are never captured as store screenshots.

THE FOUNDER'S SCREENSHOT IDEA becomes the App Store screenshots, made by web/e2e/store-shots.mjs from the same stories:
- 'Calories and protein before you order';
- 'Recipes from your supermarket, priced per serving';
- 'Plan your week on one shopping list', captioned as part of Premium (2.3.2);
- 'Your day at a glance'.
Those shots carry no logos and no chain photos (CLAUDE.md). They also leave out recipe illustrations, because out of context on the store page an AI picture of food could be taken for a photo of a product (rule 2). Real prices may appear, with the shelf-price line visible. Scan your food has no shot, because it would need a food photo.

KEEPING THEM TRUE
- N is fixed for each run before step 1 (11, or 10 for a signed-in run). A screen whose data fails keeps its place and shows one plain line, so the counter never changes.
- Next is always enabled.
- Website loads: the four candidate menus after step 2, a shop's file when it is ticked, and the week once the targets screen has drawn (chunked, 600 ms after a change, never while typing). The service worker already keeps /groceries/* and /menus/* after the first fetch.
- In the iPhone app the files are inside the app. A shop that web/app-content.json leaves unpacked would load from the live site and use the website's caps.
- Data tests in npm test, against public/menus and the shop files:
  - tests/showcaseData.test.ts proves every goal × diet (vegan, vegetarian, pescatarian, halal) × common allergen gives 2 real mains (never a side, sauce, drink, kids' dish, sharing box or limited-time item) or the plain line, and that the fallback list is named;
  - a week test proves every goal × diet × common allergen × recipe shop gives a full 7-day week or the words-only form;
  - every offered recipe shop gives two recipes.
- A unit test ties every Free tag, Premium badge and named tool to GATING_ENABLED and PHOTO_RECIPES_ENABLED.
conclusion.sign_in:
WHERE IT GOES
'Save your plan: make your free account' is the last counted step (Step 11 of 11). It comes after the three feature screens and immediately before Home. Everyone still signs in before reaching any page of the app (CLAUDE.md rule 4, unchanged).

This deliberately refines the change approved on 19 November ('straight after Your daily targets', with the shops question after it). The shops question now comes at step 4, and the week sits between the targets and the account, so the account protects something the person has just watched being built. The reasons:
- Apple's guidance to delay sign-in and ask for it in exchange for value;
- the gains other apps report from asking later;
- 'Save your plan' finally has a visible plan behind it.
This is recorded in docs/PROGRESS_LOG.md as the room's decision, and the comments in signInGate.ts, SignInScreen.tsx and tour.ts are rewritten to match.

SYNC (unchanged)
- A brand-new account keeps TYPED_SETUP_KEYS (goal, targets, glp1MealCap, preferences, shops); shops is already in the list. An existing account's own settings always win (reconcileValue).
- The body answers never leave the page's memory.
- The showcase writes nothing to the log, favourites, shopping list, saved recipes or my recipes.

PLUMBING THAT DOES CHANGE (both drafts wrongly said none did)
- afterSignIn('setup') goes to Home, not 'shops'. It keeps the restore of what was typed when signing in emptied the phone, and runs the shared finish bookkeeping.
- The 'look' reason is removed from SIGN_IN_REASONS, SIGN_IN_HEADING and PIP_LINE, and so are the FORK resume and page.tsx's restore of step TARGETS. An old tab's resume note that says 'look' now fails sanitizeResume and simply lands on the cover.
- PIP_LINE.setup becomes 'Your goal and daily numbers are ready. Your free account keeps them, and your meals and lists, safe if you change phone.'
- The navigation hints (firstRecipeId, and firstDish as {chainId, itemId}) are kept in page memory and in a new local key, mm.v1.welcomeProgress, together with the step reached. That key is not synced, not in OWN_DATA_KEYS or SYNC_STORES, and not cleared by prepareFor. They also go into SignInResume, so the website's Apple and Google redirect keeps them.
- After sign-in settles, Home's Start here note is made from them. The dish and recipe are first checked again against the account's own diet and allergens, then the progress key is deleted. This also covers the iPhone app's email-code trip: if iOS ends the web view while the person is in Mail, the relaunch goes cover › 'Carry on from step 11' › this screen, with nothing lost.

ONE FINISH FOR EVERY ENDING
After sign-in, after 'Not now' (optional mode) and at the end of a signed-in run, one function does what finish() does today:
- holdTrialOfferThisVisit();
- hasCompletedOnboarding: true;
- tourStore.set(TOUR_VERSION), now 2;
- the coach state, with no afterTour;
- the Start here note;
- clearing the progress key.
So trialOfferDue's onboarded, tourSeen and setUpThisVisit stay right.

ALREADY SIGNED IN
- Who: a Settings rerun, an account not yet set up that signed in from the cover, someone who signed in at a page's gate after opening a link, or optional mode after a Settings sign-in.
- What changes: the run has 10 steps, fixed before step 1 ('Step n of 10', Pip says '10 short steps'). Step 10's button reads 'Save and go to Home', and step 3's link reads 'Skip the rest and go to Home'.
- Nothing asks for an account the person already has.

WAYS IN AND OUT
- Returning people: the cover's 'Already have an account? Sign in' opens 'Welcome back. Sign in'. An account already set up goes straight to Home with its own settings and the toast 'Signed in. Your saved settings are back.'
- Someone who leaves mid-way (steps 2 to 11): goal, foods avoided, shops and targets are saved on each Continue, as built. The step reached is saved in mm.v1.welcomeProgress, so a plain launch reopens the cover with 'Carry on from step {n}' (step 6 if they left during the body questions).
- tourDue still reopens the flow on a plain launch while nobody is signed in where sign-in is required. TOUR_GATE_SCRIPT must still match tourDue.
- Link arrivals: nothing sends anyone to /app/welcome?next= since commit f31474f6, so afterOnboarding(), `arrival` and the ?next= handling are deleted as dead code. A shared list, friend invite, restaurant or dish link opens behind AppShell's page gate ('Sign in or sign up', as built). On their next plain launch, if they haven't set up and have nothing of their own stored, the welcome flow runs as a signed-in run of 10 steps. If they have saved something, Home opens with the existing setup cards.
- Sign out (AccountSection, to /app/welcome): the cover's Get started takes a set-up, signed-out person to 'Welcome back. Sign in' (as built).
- Delete my account: goes to /app/welcome?deleted=1 with 'Your account has been deleted. What was on this phone is still here.' A new account made later keeps what is on the phone, as any sign-in on a phone with data does (the founder's 17 November rule that the data stays).
- Clear everything: also clears mm.v1.welcomeProgress and the Start here note.
- Offline at step 11: the screen says so before any tap and keeps the answers on the phone (it was a dead end before).

THE SIGN-IN SCREEN ITSELF
- Apple first, Google at the same size, then the email code, all visible without scrolling (4.8). After sign-in, nothing more is asked: straight to Home.
- 5.1.1(v) fallback: the same screen gains only 'Not now' when numbite.com's signInOptional switch or NEXT_PUBLIC_SIGN_IN_REQUIRED=0 is on. A rejection then flips a switch rather than forcing a redesign.
- The room says plainly that the showcase does not lower the 5.1.1(v) risk, because a reviewer judges access to menus, not marketing.
- 'Delete my account' stays inside the app.
- Nothing here touches build 7 in review.

KEPT: six questions about the person, one per screen, nothing pre-picked. Each visibly changes the next screen or the one after:
1. What's your goal? (step 1): picks the step 3 list, the targets and GLP-1's meal size, and shows GLP1_NOTE for GLP-1.
2. Anything you avoid? (step 2): filters every dish, recipe and the week, and the feature screens say what was left out.
3. Where do you shop? (step 4): moved up from after sign-in. It prices the recipes on step 5 and the week on step 10, and each shop now says in advance what Numbite has for it.
4. About you (step 6): sex and age.
5. Your height and weight (step 7): stone and pounds and feet and inches by default.
6. How active are you? (step 8): with the existing everyday examples, and 'Last question.'

Steps 6 to 8 can be skipped together with one 'Skip these questions' link, and the answers are used once and never kept. 'Your daily targets' (step 9) is the editable reveal, not a question.

CALORIE-NUMBER ROUTE, WITH NO NEW SCREEN: About you gains one sentence, 'Already have a daily calorie number? Skip these questions and type it in on the next screen.' ORDER: the fast taps come first (goal, foods avoided, a restaurant, the shop, recipes) and the typing comes later, just before the reveal it pays for. So the first value arrives before the costliest 17 touches.

SAME WORD, SAME MEANING
- The top-right white 'Skip' appears only on the question screens (steps 1, 2 and 4) and always means 'skip this question'.
- The feature screens have no top-right pill; Next is always enabled.
- The body screens' skip is the 'Skip these questions' link.

It only jumps forward: 'Skip these questions' and under 18 go from 6 to 9, and step 3's link goes to 11. Pip's first line uses the same digit, and VoiceOver reads it with each headline.

TOUCHES

- About 26 touches from cover to Home with everything typed and Sign in with Apple.
- About 14 with the body questions skipped.
- 5 via step 3's link.

NEVER ASKED IN ONBOARDING

- 'What would you like help with?'.
